cells.tense: Right now the middle of this exchange is steady, and you can feel where it needs a touch.
cells.ask: Steady one exchange that still leans: make the small give or return that squares it, then keep your hands off and trust a thing once set to stay set.
cells.core:
You notice early when something between people leans — a borrowed weight, a thank-you still owed — and you make the small move that squares it. What goes out and what comes back sit level in your hands, without a score kept anywhere. People leave steadier than they arrived, and they rarely know why.

For an exchange still leaning, hold the squared shape steady. Make the one small give or the one small return that levels it, then leave the new shape alone. That is harder than the first correction: it asks you to trust that a thing once set stays set. Evenness here is not a single event you complete. It is a shape you keep, the way you keep your breath level underwater.

cells.tense: By the time the exchange arrives, you will already be at its far end, braced for a return that has not happened.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Carry your own share of one exchange, all of it, and for a stretch after, keep going on what you have without reaching over to their side for a reckoning.
cells.core:
Most exchanges you can feel the shape of before they begin — who gave what, what it adds to, what the next move should be. So you live a step ahead: what will come back, who will owe, what the payment ought to look like. Your feel for the moment is still there, but every exchange arrives with the sum already written on it.

What brings you back is carrying your own side and nothing else. Choose one exchange that matters, give what you mean to give, then go on with your day for a stretch without a check, a correction, or a weighing of what is owed. Notice what the space does. Your share is yours to carry. It does not need a verdict attached to it to be real.

cells.tense: You stopped reaching for the exchange at some point; the one here now runs on a reading you took earlier.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Sort what truly matters in one exchange from what does not — two careful columns on paper — and let a single line point to your next move.
cells.core:
You can still feel it moving between people. But the exchange on the table has gone still — not because the sense is gone, but because you have stopped reaching for it. Fairness arrives as obligation: what you owe, what is owed you. The live part of you that used to weigh it is not stepping in.

A careful walk through one exchange brings it back. Take one that has gone flat, give it attention on paper, and set down what matters in it and what does not — two columns, no rush. The line between them is the muscle you stopped using. One entry reaches the living part of you and shows you the next move. Practice does this without force; it sharpens the eye, not the nerves.

cells.tense: You are keeping exchanges level right now, and you are the only one not naming it.
cells.act: write both sides of it on one page and close the page
cells.ask: Write both sides of one exchange you have leveled — what you gave, what you took — on a single page, close the page, and do nothing else. Let your own hand show.
cells.core:
You notice when something between people tips and you bring it back before anyone falls — a small weight moved, a moment of give. The people on either side of that exchange have not seen your hand in it, and they do not need to. What only you do not see: you narrate as if you were not part of it.

Write both sides of one exchange you have leveled — what you gave, what you took — on a single page, and close the page. That is the whole ask. The truth is quieter than the story you have been running about staying out of it. Nobody is asking you to take credit. Only to see the work the way anyone else at the table already does.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange is level. You are the one holding it.
